findings.where: Article specimen, the heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' at desktop, against the hero heading 'Mark M. Moseley, infrastructure advisor'
findings.fault: The two headings use very different line spacing. The hero is set tight, about one line of space per line of type. The article heading is smaller but sits two ruled lines apart, so its two lines read as two separate lines of text, not one title. It also breaks 'Public-' / 'Private' across that wide gap. This goes against the tile's own spec, 'Bold 64/64 for headings'. At phone width the same heading is set tight, so it doesn't even match itself across widths.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reading a blog post, and the layout round that has to build article pages from this tile: the two heading styles disagree, so the tile doesn't settle how a heading is set.

findings.where: Small text set at the full 32 px rule spacing: the palette's stand-in note, the texture caption, both type-pair captions and the motion sketch's easing line and total line, at both widths (worst in the type-pair captions)
findings.fault: Text at about 15–16 px is double-spaced so its lines fall on the 32 px rules. That is more than twice the type size. A two- or three-line caption breaks into lines that look like separate notes, and the eye loses its place at each line break. The motion table beside it is set at normal tight spacing, so like text is set unlike within one panel.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder reading the tile to choose a direction, and Angélique, whose captions and small print would inherit this. The look sells 'every text block on the rules', but at caption size that makes the text harder to read, not calmer.

findings.where: Article specimen, the handwritten pull quote '“Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!”' (worst at phone width, where it runs four lines over most of a screen)
findings.fault: Mark's hand is used for a long pull quote at large size and double rule spacing. The type-pair card itself limits the hand to 'one note per view, the call to action in the margin, never body text'. An article view that also shows the 'Write to me' margin note would have two hand notes. The quote's scattered, widely spaced lines in a casual script are the most prominent type on the article and outweigh its heading.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader of Mark's article: the joke line, in a hand they can't read quickly, shouts louder than the title. The founder would object too, since the tile breaks its own rule for the hand, which leaves the layout round unsure where the script is allowed.

findings.where: Article specimen, the download row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge' / 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF', at both widths
findings.fault: The link title is set apart only by bold. The row's bottom rule runs under its last line and on under the date column, touching the descenders. It reads as a table border, not as an underline marking the title as the link. The meta column also wraps awkwardly, leaving '2026 · PDF' on a line of its own at desktop and three broken lines at phone.
findings.who_objects: A reader looking for Mark's lecture PDF: nothing in how the title is set says 'download this', and the wrapped date reads as debris.
